summary.text: A 4-year-1-month-old girl with no remarkable medical or family history presented to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of abdominal pain, vomiting and new-onset fever, with right iliac fossa tenderness and stable vital signs.

CRP was 23.1 mg/L, WBC 16.5 x 10^3 cells/uL and neutrophils 14.4 x 10^3 cells/uL. Ultrasound was inconclusive and CT showed dilated small bowel loops in the right iliac fossa, numerous large mesenteric lymph nodes and mild free fluid without confirming or excluding appendicitis.

Diagnostic laparoscopy with appendectomy found no macroscopic appendicitis and a normal-appearing appendix, but erythema and seemingly vasculitic changes in one ileal segment with the rest of the bowel normal. Histopathology showed no appendicitis and findings consistent with benign reactive follicular hyperplasia.

She was discharged the next day after symptom resolution and a negative fecal calprotectin, then readmitted 4 days later with persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting and inability to tolerate food, and a new mild purpuric rash and petechiae on the legs. CRP rose to 48.1 mg/L.

Readmission tests showed WBC 14.86 x 10^3 cells/uL within range, C3 1.830 g/L slightly elevated, positive occult blood, albumin 35.7 g/L, IgA within normal range and MPO-ANCA and PR3-ANCA not elevated. Urinalysis and protein/creatinine ratio were within normal limits and acute renal involvement was excluded at presentation.

Corticosteroids were started and IgA vasculitis was diagnosed on clinical findings and laboratory results, with mesenteric adenitis ruled out. She recovered quickly without further bowel procedures, CRP fell to 7.4 mg/L, and she was discharged two days later with follow-up appointments planned in the coming weeks. Postoperative endoscopy was not pursued.

article_limitations: Single case report; all patient facts come from one narrative plus Tables 2 to 4 and figure captions.
Table 1 is titled as causes of nonimmune hydrops fetalis but lists IgA vasculitis classification criteria from a pediatrics text; it is treated as background reference content, not patient data.
The Discussion mentions perioperative corticosteroid administration that the case narrative does not report; agent, dose and route are unknown.
Dates are not stated; relative timing is kept as written (24-hour history, next day, 4 days after discharge, two days later).
The text contains the stray sentence All figures should be included here, which carries no clinical content.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the five JPEG figures are inspected in the separate visual submission.
The Figure 1 CT pixels carry a printed acquisition date and time that the text does not state; it is not used as a patient fact.
